No coaching, hints, scored-result disclosure, or targeted practice may occur between a passing PRIMARY and its CONFIRMATION. Both valid forms must satisfy the same RS P10 readiness rule. If PRIMARY fails, stop the cycle and remediate before a new cycle. If PRIMARY passes but CONFIRMATION fails, mark DISCORDANT_NOT_YET and remediate before a new cycle. Technical-invalid forms are REASSESS_TECHNICAL and do not count as valid attempts. All valid forms remain in the audit record; the system may never cherry-pick the best historical pass.
matched_form_equivalence_policy: EQUIV-2.1: exact 100 COUNT-100 words; World 1 one-word display; same RS/P10, scoring version, threshold version/status, comprehension blueprint class and safety/accessibility gates; fresh unseen content; non-compensatory global + RS-specific matching; candidate must pass all tolerances embedded in the canonical v0.22 Markdown specification.
readiness_attempt_policy: ATTEMPT-1.0: A readiness cycle is PRIMARY→CONFIRMATION. A valid failure ends that cycle. A new cycle may begin only after an intervening targeted learning block for that RS. After two consecutive failed/discordant valid cycles, set DIAGNOSTIC_HOLD and require at least two targeted non-readiness practice passages plus a documented diagnostic review before another readiness cycle. There is no unlimited back-to-back retry loop. Genuine later learning may reopen assessment after the required learning block.
readiness_cycle_status_rule: Readiness-cycle states: PRIMARY_PENDING; CONFIRMATION_PENDING; CONFIRMED_READY; NOT_YET; DISCORDANT_NOT_YET; REASSESS_TECHNICAL; INVALID_FORM; DIAGNOSTIC_HOLD. Only CONFIRMED_READY counts as resolved readiness for the RS (subject to RS07 evidence-path semantics and threshold lifecycle).
band_a_remediation_rule: After a valid failed/discordant cycle, remediate only that RS before a new cycle. The new cycle must use two fresh unseen EQUIV-2.1 matched P10 forms. After two consecutive failed/discordant cycles, enter DIAGNOSTIC_HOLD and require at least two targeted non-readiness practice passages plus diagnostic review before another readiness cycle.
personal_progress_measure: Primary comparison: RS10-P1 → RS10-P5. Report only this learner's within-competency metric changes; comprehension remains a separate measure. Cross-RS raw comparisons are prohibited.
hook_requirement: Open within first 25 words using puzzle breakthrough or an equally strong curiosity trigger; do not explain the lesson up front.
mid_passage_pull: By roughly the midpoint, introduce a change, clue, consequence, question or small complication so curiosity remains active.
ending_payoff: Resolve the passage cleanly in the final ~20 words; leave satisfaction, wonder or a useful thought—never a sermon or forced moral.
engagement_qa: Score Hook 0–2 + Mid-pull 0–2 + Payoff 0–2. Passage prose must score ≥5/6 and may not score 0 in any dimension.
qa_gate_definition: AMBIGUITY/FACT CONSISTENCY GATE: Every factual statement must be internally consistent with the premise and quiz. Every quiz item must have one defensible answer. Remove wording that permits multiple reasonable interpretations. Names, chronology, quantities, cause/effect and stated motivations must not contradict one another.
band_a_oral_readiness_rule: BAND-A ORAL READINESS (self-contained): readiness uses all RS01-P10…RS15-P10. Required P10 rules are the RS-specific success rules in this file. Core integrated minimums include: RS01 final_accuracy ≥97% and first_pass_accuracy ≥95%; RS02 ≤2 sequence errors with no 2+ word skip; RS06 ≤3 >2-second hesitations and no unexplained silence >6 s; RS08 ≤2 unnecessary repetition events and ≤1 full restart; RS11 pace_spread ≤0.25; RS13 middle-third accuracy within 2 percentage points of first-third with no 2+ word skip; RS14 final-third accuracy within 2 percentage points of first-third and final-third WPM no more than 15% below first-third; RS15 final_accuracy ≥95%, sequence_errors ≤2, long hesitations ≤4, full_restarts ≤1 and pace_spread ≤0.25. All remaining RS03–RS05, RS07, RS09–RS10 and RS12 P10 rules are equally mandatory; none may be bypassed by averaging.
factual_safety_requirement: AMBIGUITY/FACT CONSISTENCY GATE: Every factual statement must be internally consistent with the premise and quiz. Every quiz item must have one defensible answer. Remove wording that permits multiple reasonable interpretations. Names, chronology, quantities, cause/effect and stated motivations must not contradict one another.
babysteps_rule: Effortless learning: engaging first, gentle stretch, useful idea, no preaching, high chance of success.
prose_content_fidelity_rule: CONTENT FIDELITY: Preserve the row's core premise, knowledge strand, comprehension target, wisdom/trait intent, hook/pull/payoff intent, setting-accessibility requirement and QA flags. Prose may creatively realize the row, but it may not silently replace the learning objective.
prose_comprehension_evidence_rule: P5 FEELINGS/MOTIVATION: behaviour/context must support one primary feeling or motivation; avoid mixed cues that make two answers equally valid.
prose_oral_compatibility_rule: RS10 INTERNAL PUNCTUATION: include at least 3 natural eligible internal punctuation opportunities (primarily commas) without comma stuffing.
prose_speech_fairness_rule: SPEECH/ACCENT FAIRNESS: The passage must be comfortable to read aloud by a beginner. Reject tongue-twister construction, dense alliteration, repeated minimal-pair traps, unnatural consonant clusters, clusters of difficult proper nouns, or wording chosen mainly to provoke ASR failure. Accent variation must not be used as a test. Names should be short/easy unless the passage itself gently teaches the name.
prose_vocabulary_rule: CONTROLLED STRETCH VOCABULARY: Most words must be familiar/decodable for a beginner reader. Stretch words must be intentional, context-supported and sparse enough that they do not break flow. Do not stack multiple unfamiliar words in one sentence. Writer-tagged RS05/RS12 targets count as the deliberate stretch; do not add extra difficult vocabulary merely to sound sophisticated.
prose_wisdom_rule: IMPLICIT WISDOM: The registry may name a trait or wisdom goal, but the prose should normally let it emerge from events, choices and consequences. Avoid formulaic moral endings such as 'X learned that...', 'X understood that...' or direct lectures unless the row specifically requires explicit explanation. A passage may be funny, mysterious, beautiful or surprising without stating a moral.
prose_duplicate_rule: NEARBY-DUPLICATE GATE: QA is performed in actual delivery-session order, not passage-ID order. Within the previous and next 15 delivered sessions, reject a near-duplicate core plot/event structure. A wisdom trait may recur only when conflict, setting and outcome are materially different. A hook type may recur only when the story/problem experience is clearly different. No passage may substantially duplicate the combination of plot + lesson/insight + hook/pull pattern of a nearby passage.
prose_confidence_rule: FIRST-100 CONFIDENCE PROTECTION (Sessions 61–80 — I’m getting better): the passage must feel achievable on first encounter. No trick comprehension, humiliation/failure language, sudden difficulty spike, dense unfamiliar vocabulary, or punitive reread. Introduce at most one main new challenge beyond what the current RS/P cell requires. Feedback/remediation should preserve the learner's sense of 'I can do this' and desire for the next passage.
prose_wordcount_rhythm_rule: 100-WORD NATURALNESS: Final learner-visible prose must be exactly 100 words under the project's word-count convention, but exact count never justifies filler, clipped grammar, repeated meaning, awkward connectors, distorted facts, or unnatural oral rhythm. If the natural version is not 100 words, rewrite structurally rather than padding.
prose_quiz_path_rule: QUIZ/COMPREHENSION PATH: The finished passage and quiz must support exactly one defensible keyed answer per scored item. The intended evidence path must be visible in the text or strongly supported by it. Reject trick wording, unsupported inference, multiple reasonable answers, or a quiz whose correct answer depends on outside knowledge.
prose_effortless_learning_rule: BABYSTEPS EFFORTLESS-LEARNING GATE: The child should experience a worthwhile story/idea, not a disguised worksheet. Reading practice, vocabulary, wisdom and comprehension training should remain mostly invisible inside an engaging passage. A passage that is educational but dull, or entertaining but leaves no meaningful reading/comprehension value, fails.
prose_generation_gate_summary: PASS ONLY IF content fidelity + comprehension evidence + RS oral compatibility + speech/accent fairness + controlled vocabulary + implicit wisdom + nearby-duplicate check + confidence protection + exact-100 natural rhythm + one-defensible-answer quiz path + effortless-learning + engagement + all applicable factual/safety gates pass.
form_profile_lock_rule: P10 PRIMARY profile is frozen after prose QA and before learner exposure; CONFIRMATION must pass MFORM-1.1 against the frozen profile before delivery.
form_family_production_requirement: Production readiness requires the relevant RS P10 form family to be PRODUCTION_APPROVED in addition to individual candidate STRUCTURAL_EQUIV_PASS.
readiness_freshness_rule: Readiness evidence remains CURRENT until the first of: >56 calendar days since the latest passing same-RS confirmation/revalidation; >16 subsequent valid Band-A assessment/remediation sessions; or >28 consecutive calendar days with no SpeedReader learning session. reading_behavior_target: The learner makes a shorter internal pause at commas where appropriate, then continues the same sentence without losing place. Current P8 demand: ≥72%.
oral_alignment_rule: OS1 ALIGNMENT: Score against learner-visible passage words in order. Normalize case and typographic apostrophes; retain punctuation separately for punctuation scoring. Use word-level sequence alignment over expected tokens and spoken lexical tokens. Non-lexical filled pauses such as 'um'/'uh' are hesitation events, not insertions. Approved lexical equivalents must be declared before scoring. A low-confidence ASR mismatch is UNRESOLVED, not automatically a child error.
oral_accuracy_rule: OS2 ACCURACY: first_pass_accuracy = first-pass correct assessable expected words / assessable expected words. final_accuracy = expected words correct after accepted self-corrections / assessable expected words. A self-corrected word remains wrong for first-pass accuracy but becomes correct for final accuracy; the self-correction is also logged separately. Unresolved ASR tokens are excluded from both numerator and denominator until resolved.
oral_error_event_rule: OS3 ERROR EVENTS: substitution = first lexical attempt differs from expected token and is not an approved equivalent; omission = expected token has no aligned lexical attempt before the learner progresses beyond it; insertion = extra lexical token not aligned to any expected token; repetition = already-read expected word/phrase spoken again without textual need. A repeat used only to make an accepted self-correction is not an unnecessary repetition.
oral_self_correction_rule: OS4 SELF-CORRECTION: accepted when, without an app prompt, the learner replaces a confirmed misread/omission with the intended expected word within 5.0 seconds of the first erroneous attempt and before progressing more than 2 expected words beyond the target. Record correction_latency_seconds. The event still counts as a first-pass error, but the target counts correct in final_accuracy. RS07 may impose its stricter P-level latency/success threshold on top of this general acceptance rule.
oral_hesitation_rule: OS5 HESITATION: a long hesitation is a non-punctuation silence >2.0 seconds between assessable lexical events while the learner has not intentionally stopped. Measure from offset of the previous spoken lexical token to onset of the next spoken lexical token. Exclude permitted punctuation pauses, app/system audio, invalid recording gaps and ASR-uncertain spans. Filled pauses ('um', 'uh') extend the hesitation interval but are not insertions.
oral_restart_rule: OS6 FULL RESTART: after progressing at least 3 expected words into the current sentence, the learner returns to the sentence's first expected word or to an earlier sentence, producing a backward alignment jump of at least 3 expected tokens, without an app prompt. Repeating/correcting only 1–2 expected tokens is a local correction/repetition, not a full restart.
oral_punctuation_rule: OS7 PUNCTUATION: terminal eligible marks (. ? !) are compliant when the pause from final-word offset to next-word onset is 0.150–1.800 s and the next sentence begins without a boundary-linked omission. terminal_compliance = compliant eligible terminal marks / eligible terminal marks. Internal eligible marks (primarily comma, colon, semicolon) are compliant when the pause is 0.080–0.900 s and reading continues within the same sentence without a punctuation-triggered full restart. internal_compliance = compliant eligible internal marks / eligible internal marks. Exclude abbreviations, quoted punctuation or marks pre-tagged by the writer as non-pause-eligible.
oral_recovery_rule: OS8 CHALLENGE/UNFAMILIAR-WORD RECOVERY: computed only for writer-tagged recovery targets. recovery_time_seconds runs from onset of the learner's first attempt at the target to offset of the first accepted correct production. A target is recovered when it is correct or accepted-self-corrected within that RS/P time limit and the next 5 expected words contain no more than the allowed sequence errors and no target-triggered full restart. If the target is omitted with no attempt, recovery fails. If ASR is unresolved on the target, status is REASSESS rather than fail.
oral_wpm_rule: OS9 TIME/WPM: reading_time starts at onset of the first assessable passage word and ends at offset of the final assessable expected word reached. Include genuine hesitations, repetitions, self-corrections and restarts because they consume reading time; exclude app prompts/system audio and invalid recording gaps. text_WPM = number of expected passage words successfully progressed through / active elapsed reading minutes. Do not use total spoken-token count, because repetitions/insertions must not inflate WPM.
oral_asr_rule: OS10 ASR/ACCENT SAFEGUARD: ASR is evidence, not ground truth. Accent variation alone is never an error. A mismatch may be auto-scored as a child error only when the recognizer's confidence for the mismatching lexical hypothesis is at or above the engine's calibrated HIGH_CONFIDENCE threshold and no approved pronunciation/lexical equivalent applies. Lower-confidence mismatches are UNRESOLVED and excluded from scoring until a secondary recognition pass or replay resolves them. The deployed engine must freeze and version its HIGH_CONFIDENCE threshold; changing that threshold changes the scoring version.
oral_sample_validity_rule: OS11 SAMPLE VALIDITY: a metric is computable only when enough eligible evidence exists for that metric. title: Copying the Homework
strand_goal: Build curiosity, practice habits, asking questions and learning from mistakes.
passage_premise: Sam forgot one answer and has the chance to copy before class begins.
wisdom_or_trait: A small honest mistake teaches more than a copied success.
wisdom_delivery: Implicit through events/consequences; do not end with “learned/realised/understood that…” unless natural to the story.
comprehension_target: Judge a simple choice and transfer the idea to a new but similar situation.
quiz_blueprint: Compare consequences: Choose which of two actions better avoids the stated negative consequence.
quiz_mastery_rule: First-attempt mastery = at least 2/3 and the designated primary-skill item correct. Otherwise remediate only the missed skill and ask one fresh item. During delivery Sessions 1–100, never show a failure label; oral speed/accuracy coaches but does not block progression.
comprehension_independent_first_attempt_: Not a P10 final-readiness form; use normal instructional comprehension progression.
comprehension_confirmation_rule: Not required for this non-P10 passage.
comprehension_readiness_status_rule: Not a Band-A comprehension certification row.
band_a_comprehension_gate: Does not directly close Band-A comprehension readiness.
reading_skill_step: RS10/P9 — Internal-punctuation control: ≥76% with zero punctuation-triggered full restart.
reading_behavior_target: The learner makes a shorter internal pause at commas where appropriate, then continues the same sentence without losing place. Current P9 demand: ≥76% with zero punctuation-triggered full restart.
oral_alignment_rule: OS1 ALIGNMENT: Score against learner-visible passage words in order. Normalize case and typographic apostrophes; retain punctuation separately for punctuation scoring. Use word-level sequence alignment over expected tokens and spoken lexical tokens. Non-lexical filled pauses such as 'um'/'uh' are hesitation events, not insertions. Approved lexical equivalents must be declared before scoring. A low-confidence ASR mismatch is UNRESOLVED, not automatically a child error.
oral_accuracy_rule: OS2 ACCURACY: first_pass_accuracy = first-pass correct assessable expected words / assessable expected words. final_accuracy = expected words correct after accepted self-corrections / assessable expected words. A self-corrected word remains wrong for first-pass accuracy but becomes correct for final accuracy; the self-correction is also logged separately. Unresolved ASR tokens are excluded from both numerator and denominator until resolved.
oral_error_event_rule: OS3 ERROR EVENTS: substitution = first lexical attempt differs from expected token and is not an approved equivalent; omission = expected token has no aligned lexical attempt before the learner progresses beyond it; insertion = extra lexical token not aligned to any expected token; repetition = already-read expected word/phrase spoken again without textual need. A repeat used only to make an accepted self-correction is not an unnecessary repetition.
oral_self_correction_rule: OS4 SELF-CORRECTION: accepted when, without an app prompt, the learner replaces a confirmed misread/omission with the intended expected word within 5.0 seconds of the first erroneous attempt and before progressing more than 2 expected words beyond the target. Record correction_latency_seconds. The event still counts as a first-pass error, but the target counts correct in final_accuracy. RS07 may impose its stricter P-level latency/success threshold on top of this general acceptance rule.
oral_hesitation_rule: OS5 HESITATION: a long hesitation is a non-punctuation silence >2.0 seconds between assessable lexical events while the learner has not intentionally stopped. Measure from offset of the previous spoken lexical token to onset of the next spoken lexical token. Exclude permitted punctuation pauses, app/system audio, invalid recording gaps and ASR-uncertain spans. Filled pauses ('um', 'uh') extend the hesitation interval but are not insertions.
oral_restart_rule: OS6 FULL RESTART: after progressing at least 3 expected words into the current sentence, the learner returns to the sentence's first expected word or to an earlier sentence, producing a backward alignment jump of at least 3 expected tokens, without an app prompt. Repeating/correcting only 1–2 expected tokens is a local correction/repetition, not a full restart.
oral_punctuation_rule: OS7 PUNCTUATION: terminal eligible marks (. ? !) are compliant when the pause from final-word offset to next-word onset is 0.150–1.800 s and the next sentence begins without a boundary-linked omission. terminal_compliance = compliant eligible terminal marks / eligible terminal marks. Internal eligible marks (primarily comma, colon, semicolon) are compliant when the pause is 0.080–0.900 s and reading continues within the same sentence without a punctuation-triggered full restart. internal_compliance = compliant eligible internal marks / eligible internal marks. Exclude abbreviations, quoted punctuation or marks pre-tagged by the writer as non-pause-eligible.
oral_recovery_rule: OS8 CHALLENGE/UNFAMILIAR-WORD RECOVERY: computed only for writer-tagged recovery targets. recovery_time_seconds runs from onset of the learner's first attempt at the target to offset of the first accepted correct production. A target is recovered when it is correct or accepted-self-corrected within that RS/P time limit and the next 5 expected words contain no more than the allowed sequence errors and no target-triggered full restart. If the target is omitted with no attempt, recovery fails. If ASR is unresolved on the target, status is REASSESS rather than fail.
oral_wpm_rule: OS9 TIME/WPM: reading_time starts at onset of the first assessable passage word and ends at offset of the final assessable expected word reached. Include genuine hesitations, repetitions, self-corrections and restarts because they consume reading time; exclude app prompts/system audio and invalid recording gaps. text_WPM = number of expected passage words successfully progressed through / active elapsed reading minutes. Do not use total spoken-token count, because repetitions/insertions must not inflate WPM.
oral_asr_rule: OS10 ASR/ACCENT SAFEGUARD: ASR is evidence, not ground truth. Accent variation alone is never an error. A mismatch may be auto-scored as a child error only when the recognizer's confidence for the mismatching lexical hypothesis is at or above the engine's calibrated HIGH_CONFIDENCE threshold and no approved pronunciation/lexical equivalent applies. Lower-confidence mismatches are UNRESOLVED and excluded from scoring until a secondary recognition pass or replay resolves them. The deployed engine must freeze and version its HIGH_CONFIDENCE threshold; changing that threshold changes the scoring version.
oral_sample_validity_rule: OS11 SAMPLE VALIDITY: a metric is computable only when enough eligible evidence exists for that metric. If microphone dropout, clipping, overlapping speech, system narration or unresolved ASR removes >10% of expected words from assessability, the oral sample is INVALID for readiness scoring and must be reassessed. For a targeted metric requiring a minimum number of tagged opportunities, insufficient eligible targets yields REASSESS, not PASS or FAIL.
oral_pipeline_order: OS12 PIPELINE ORDER: (1) validate audio/sample; (2) tokenize/normalize expected text; (3) align spoken lexical events; (4) mark substitutions/omissions/insertions/repetitions; (5) determine accepted self-corrections; (6) compute first_pass_accuracy and final_accuracy; (7) compute timing, hesitation, restart, punctuation, WPM and recovery metrics; (8) apply the assigned RS/P success rule; (9) apply ASR uncertainty/REASSESS rules before any readiness decision.
rs_progress_comparison: Compare only RS10-P9 with RS10-P1 baseline (Session 010) and, for short-term trend, RS10-P8 (Session 115). Never compare raw values with a different RS competency.
progress_display_rule: Child-facing progress uses native within-RS changes (for example accuracy +4 percentage points, hesitations 7→3, pace spread 0.42→0.28). Do not show one raw cross-RS 'improved by X%' score.
normalized_composite_rule: Optional full-round composite only after all 15 RS tracks have completed the same P level. For each required metric, normalize progress as target-gap closure from that RS's own P1 baseline toward its P10 target; metrics already meeting target at P1 are tagged 'baseline mastery' rather than treated as improvement. Combine required metrics within an RS, then combine the 15 RS normalized values. Never average raw heterogeneous metrics.
band_a_final_evidence: Canonical final Band-A oral evidence = Delivery Sessions 136–150 only as a complete set: RS01-P10 through RS15-P10. Earlier same-RS samples remain supporting trend evidence.
band_a_rs_status_rule: Use readiness_state only: PRIMARY_PENDING → PRIMARY_PASS/CONFIRMATION_PENDING → CONFIRMED_READY, or cause-specific NOT_YET / DISCORDANT_NOT_YET / REASSESS_TECHNICAL / INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE / INVALID_FORM / DIAGNOSTIC_HOLD. Only CONFIRMED_READY initially closes readiness; BASELINE_MASTERY is progress reporting only.
band_a_readiness_gate: Band-A oral readiness requires all 15 RS readiness_state values to be CONFIRMED_READY (or CURRENT_REVALIDATED after prior confirmed readiness), plus BAND_A_COMPREHENSION_READY and current recency evidence. Progress descriptors—including BASELINE_MASTERY—never satisfy the readiness gate.
p10_confirmation_policy: CONFIRM-1.0: A single valid P10 pass never closes an RS. Each RS readiness cycle uses two fresh unseen equivalent P10 forms: PRIMARY then CONFIRMATION. No coaching, hints, scored-result disclosure, or targeted practice may occur between a passing PRIMARY and its CONFIRMATION. Both valid forms must satisfy the same RS P10 readiness rule. If PRIMARY fails, stop the cycle and remediate before a new cycle. If PRIMARY passes but CONFIRMATION fails, mark DISCORDANT_NOT_YET and remediate before a new cycle. Technical-invalid forms are REASSESS_TECHNICAL and do not count as valid attempts. All valid forms remain in the audit record; the system may never cherry-pick the best historical pass.
matched_form_equivalence_policy: EQUIV-2.1: exact 100 COUNT-100 words; World 1 one-word display; same RS/P10, scoring version, threshold version/status, comprehension blueprint class and safety/accessibility gates; fresh unseen content; non-compensatory global + RS-specific matching; candidate must pass all tolerances embedded in the canonical v0.22 Markdown specification.
readiness_attempt_policy: ATTEMPT-1.0: A readiness cycle is PRIMARY→CONFIRMATION. A valid failure ends that cycle. A new cycle may begin only after an intervening targeted learning block for that RS. After two consecutive failed/discordant valid cycles, set DIAGNOSTIC_HOLD and require at least two targeted non-readiness practice passages plus a documented diagnostic review before another readiness cycle. There is no unlimited back-to-back retry loop. Genuine later learning may reopen assessment after the required learning block.
readiness_cycle_status_rule: Readiness-cycle states: PRIMARY_PENDING; CONFIRMATION_PENDING; CONFIRMED_READY; NOT_YET; DISCORDANT_NOT_YET; REASSESS_TECHNICAL; INVALID_FORM; DIAGNOSTIC_HOLD. Only CONFIRMED_READY counts as resolved readiness for the RS (subject to RS07 evidence-path semantics and threshold lifecycle).
band_a_remediation_rule: After a valid failed/discordant cycle, remediate only that RS before a new cycle. The new cycle must use two fresh unseen EQUIV-2.1 matched P10 forms. After two consecutive failed/discordant cycles, enter DIAGNOSTIC_HOLD and require at least two targeted non-readiness practice passages plus diagnostic review before another readiness cycle.
personal_progress_measure: Primary comparison: RS10-P1 → RS10-P9. Report only this learner's within-competency metric changes; comprehension remains a separate measure. Cross-RS raw comparisons are prohibited.
hook_requirement: Open within first 25 words using temptation or an equally strong curiosity trigger; do not explain the lesson up front.
mid_passage_pull: By roughly the midpoint, introduce a change, clue, consequence, question or small complication so curiosity remains active.
ending_payoff: Resolve the passage cleanly in the final ~20 words; leave satisfaction, wonder or a useful thought—never a sermon or forced moral.
engagement_qa: Score Hook 0–2 + Mid-pull 0–2 + Payoff 0–2. Passage prose must score ≥5/6 and may not score 0 in any dimension.
qa_gate_definition: AMBIGUITY/FACT CONSISTENCY GATE: Every factual statement must be internally consistent with the premise and quiz. Every quiz item must have one defensible answer. Remove wording that permits multiple reasonable interpretations. Names, chronology, quantities, cause/effect and stated motivations must not contradict one another.
band_a_oral_readiness_rule: BAND-A ORAL READINESS (self-contained): readiness uses all RS01-P10…RS15-P10. Required P10 rules are the RS-specific success rules in this file. Core integrated minimums include: RS01 final_accuracy ≥97% and first_pass_accuracy ≥95%; RS02 ≤2 sequence errors with no 2+ word skip; RS06 ≤3 >2-second hesitations and no unexplained silence >6 s; RS08 ≤2 unnecessary repetition events and ≤1 full restart; RS11 pace_spread ≤0.25; RS13 middle-third accuracy within 2 percentage points of first-third with no 2+ word skip; RS14 final-third accuracy within 2 percentage points of first-third and final-third WPM no more than 15% below first-third; RS15 final_accuracy ≥95%, sequence_errors ≤2, long hesitations ≤4, full_restarts ≤1 and pace_spread ≤0.25. All remaining RS03–RS05, RS07, RS09–RS10 and RS12 P10 rules are equally mandatory; none may be bypassed by averaging.
factual_safety_requirement: AMBIGUITY/FACT CONSISTENCY GATE: Every factual statement must be internally consistent with the premise and quiz. Every quiz item must have one defensible answer. Remove wording that permits multiple reasonable interpretations. Names, chronology, quantities, cause/effect and stated motivations must not contradict one another.
babysteps_rule: Effortless learning: engaging first, gentle stretch, useful idea, no preaching, high chance of success.
prose_content_fidelity_rule: CONTENT FIDELITY: Preserve the row's core premise, knowledge strand, comprehension target, wisdom/trait intent, hook/pull/payoff intent, setting-accessibility requirement and QA flags. Prose may creatively realize the row, but it may not silently replace the learning objective.
prose_comprehension_evidence_rule: P9 JUDGMENT/APPLICATION: constrain the scenario so one action/choice is clearly the safest, fairest or most reasonable under the passage facts; avoid opinion-only questions.
prose_oral_compatibility_rule: RS10 INTERNAL PUNCTUATION: include at least 4 natural eligible internal punctuation opportunities (primarily commas) without comma stuffing.
prose_speech_fairness_rule: SPEECH/ACCENT FAIRNESS: The passage must be comfortable to read aloud by a beginner. Reject tongue-twister construction, dense alliteration, repeated minimal-pair traps, unnatural consonant clusters, clusters of difficult proper nouns, or wording chosen mainly to provoke ASR failure. Accent variation must not be used as a test. Names should be short/easy unless the passage itself gently teaches the name.
prose_vocabulary_rule: CONTROLLED STRETCH VOCABULARY: Most words must be familiar/decodable for a beginner reader. Stretch words must be intentional, context-supported and sparse enough that they do not break flow. Do not stack multiple unfamiliar words in one sentence. Writer-tagged RS05/RS12 targets count as the deliberate stretch; do not add extra difficult vocabulary merely to sound sophisticated.
prose_wisdom_rule: IMPLICIT WISDOM: The registry may name a trait or wisdom goal, but the prose should normally let it emerge from events, choices and consequences. Avoid formulaic moral endings such as 'X learned that...', 'X understood that...' or direct lectures unless the row specifically requires explicit explanation. A passage may be funny, mysterious, beautiful or surprising without stating a moral.
prose_duplicate_rule: NEARBY-DUPLICATE GATE: QA is performed in actual delivery-session order, not passage-ID order. Within the previous and next 15 delivered sessions, reject a near-duplicate core plot/event structure. A wisdom trait may recur only when conflict, setting and outcome are materially different. A hook type may recur only when the story/problem experience is clearly different. No passage may substantially duplicate the combination of plot + lesson/insight + hook/pull pattern of a nearby passage.
prose_confidence_rule: POST-100 STRENGTHENING (Sessions 101–150 — Strengthen and prepare for 200-word endurance): challenge may increase modestly, but difficulty must still rise gradually and remain compatible with beginner one-word reading. Do not sacrifice engagement, oral naturalness or comprehension uniqueness for toughness.
prose_wordcount_rhythm_rule: 100-WORD NATURALNESS: Final learner-visible prose must be exactly 100 words under the project's word-count convention, but exact count never justifies filler, clipped grammar, repeated meaning, awkward connectors, distorted facts, or unnatural oral rhythm. If the natural version is not 100 words, rewrite structurally rather than padding.
prose_quiz_path_rule: QUIZ/COMPREHENSION PATH: The finished passage and quiz must support exactly one defensible keyed answer per scored item. The intended evidence path must be visible in the text or strongly supported by it. Reject trick wording, unsupported inference, multiple reasonable answers, or a quiz whose correct answer depends on outside knowledge.
prose_effortless_learning_rule: BABYSTEPS EFFORTLESS-LEARNING GATE: The child should experience a worthwhile story/idea, not a disguised worksheet. Reading practice, vocabulary, wisdom and comprehension training should remain mostly invisible inside an engaging passage. A passage that is educational but dull, or entertaining but leaves no meaningful reading/comprehension value, fails.
prose_generation_gate_summary: PASS ONLY IF content fidelity + comprehension evidence + RS oral compatibility + speech/accent fairness + controlled vocabulary + implicit wisdom + nearby-duplicate check + confidence protection + exact-100 natural rhythm + one-defensible-answer quiz path + effortless-learning + engagement + all applicable factual/safety gates pass.
form_profile_lock_rule: P10 PRIMARY profile is frozen after prose QA and before learner exposure; CONFIRMATION must pass MFORM-1.1 against the frozen profile before delivery.
form_family_production_requirement: Production readiness requires the relevant RS P10 form family to be PRODUCTION_APPROVED in addition to individual candidate STRUCTURAL_EQUIV_PASS.
readiness_freshness_rule: Readiness evidence remains CURRENT until the first of: >56 calendar days since the latest passing same-RS confirmation/revalidation; >16 subsequent valid Band-A assessment/remediation sessions; or >28 consecutive calendar days with no SpeedReader learning session. Material scoring/threshold-version changes invalidate evidence immediately rather than merely making it stale. These numeric limits are PROVISIONAL_PILOT and require later calibration.
readiness_revalidation_rule: When evidence is REVALIDATION_DUE only because of recency/inactivity, use one fresh unseen EQUIV-2.1 same-RS P10 revalidation form. Score oral and comprehension streams independently before any targeted feedback. A passing stream renews only that stream's freshness anchor. A valid failing stream becomes NOT_YET and requires targeted remediation followed by a new full PRIMARY→CONFIRMATION cycle for that stream. Technical invalidity does not count as failure and does not reset freshness until valid evidence is obtained.
readiness_version_invalidation_rule: If OS/scoring semantics, threshold version/status, or another material measurement definition changes incompatibly, set VERSION_INVALIDATED. Do not use the one-form recency shortcut; require a new full two-form readiness cycle under the new compatible version.
band_a_evidence_current_rule: At final closure, the oral and comprehension readiness streams associated with all 15 RS positions must be CURRENT or CURRENT_REVALIDATED.
minimum_evidence_rule: P10 readiness minimums apply only to readiness/confirmation/revalidation forms.
form_minimum_precheck_rule: For P10 readiness forms, reject before learner exposure when writer-controlled tagged/event opportunities are below EVIDENCE-MIN-1.0.

oral_accuracy_rule: OS2 ACCURACY: first_pass_accuracy = first-pass correct assessable expected words / assessable expected words. final_accuracy = expected words correct after accepted self-corrections / assessable expected words. A self-corrected word remains wrong for first-pass accuracy but becomes correct for final accuracy; the self-correction is also logged separately. Unresolved ASR tokens are excluded from both numerator and denominator until resolved.
oral_error_event_rule: OS3 ERROR EVENTS: substitution = first lexical attempt differs from expected token and is not an approved equivalent; omission = expected token has no aligned lexical attempt before the learner progresses beyond it; insertion = extra lexical token not aligned to any expected token; repetition = already-read expected word/phrase spoken again without textual need. A repeat used only to make an accepted self-correction is not an unnecessary repetition.
oral_self_correction_rule: OS4 SELF-CORRECTION: accepted when, without an app prompt, the learner replaces a confirmed misread/omission with the intended expected word within 5.0 seconds of the first erroneous attempt and before progressing more than 2 expected words beyond the target. Record correction_latency_seconds. The event still counts as a first-pass error, but the target counts correct in final_accuracy. RS07 may impose its stricter P-level latency/success threshold on top of this general acceptance rule.
oral_hesitation_rule: OS5 HESITATION: a long hesitation is a non-punctuation silence >2.0 seconds between assessable lexical events while the learner has not intentionally stopped. Measure from offset of the previous spoken lexical token to onset of the next spoken lexical token. Exclude permitted punctuation pauses, app/system audio, invalid recording gaps and ASR-uncertain spans. Filled pauses ('um', 'uh') extend the hesitation interval but are not insertions.
oral_restart_rule: OS6 FULL RESTART: after progressing at least 3 expected words into the current sentence, the learner returns to the sentence's first expected word or to an earlier sentence, producing a backward alignment jump of at least 3 expected tokens, without an app prompt. Repeating/correcting only 1–2 expected tokens is a local correction/repetition, not a full restart.
oral_punctuation_rule: OS7 PUNCTUATION: terminal eligible marks (. ? !) are compliant when the pause from final-word offset to next-word onset is 0.150–1.800 s and the next sentence begins without a boundary-linked omission. terminal_compliance = compliant eligible terminal marks / eligible terminal marks. Internal eligible marks (primarily comma, colon, semicolon) are compliant when the pause is 0.080–0.900 s and reading continues within the same sentence without a punctuation-triggered full restart. internal_compliance = compliant eligible internal marks / eligible internal marks. Exclude abbreviations, quoted punctuation or marks pre-tagged by the writer as non-pause-eligible.
oral_recovery_rule: OS8 CHALLENGE/UNFAMILIAR-WORD RECOVERY: computed only for writer-tagged recovery targets. recovery_time_seconds runs from onset of the learner's first attempt at the target to offset of the first accepted correct production. oral_wpm_rule: OS9 TIME/WPM: reading_time starts at onset of the first assessable passage word and ends at offset of the final assessable expected word reached. Unresolved ASR tokens are excluded from both numerator and denominator until resolved.
oral_error_event_rule: OS3 ERROR EVENTS: substitution = first lexical attempt differs from expected token and is not an approved equivalent; omission = expected token has no aligned lexical attempt before the learner progresses beyond it; insertion = extra lexical token not aligned to any expected token; repetition = already-read expected word/phrase spoken again without textual need. A repeat used only to make an accepted self-correction is not an unnecessary repetition.
oral_self_correction_rule: OS4 SELF-CORRECTION: accepted when, without an app prompt, the learner replaces a confirmed misread/omission with the intended expected word within 5.0 seconds of the first erroneous attempt and before progressing more than 2 expected words beyond the target. oral_hesitation_rule: OS5 HESITATION: a long hesitation is a non-punctuation silence >2.0 seconds between assessable lexical events while the learner has not intentionally stopped. Exclude permitted punctuation pauses, app/system audio, invalid recording gaps and ASR-uncertain spans. Filled pauses ('um', 'uh') extend the hesitation interval but are not insertions.
oral_restart_rule: OS6 FULL RESTART: after progressing at least 3 expected words into the current sentence, the learner returns to the sentence's first expected word or to an earlier sentence, producing a backward alignment jump of at least 3 expected tokens, without an app prompt. oral_alignment_rule: OS1 ALIGNMENT: Score against learner-visible passage words in order. Normalize case and typographic apostrophes; retain punctuation separately for punctuation scoring. Use word-level sequence alignment over expected tokens and spoken lexical tokens. Non-lexical filled pauses such as 'um'/'uh' are hesitation events, not insertions. Approved lexical equivalents must be declared before scoring. A low-confidence ASR mismatch is UNRESOLVED, not automatically a child error.
oral_accuracy_rule: OS2 ACCURACY: first_pass_accuracy = first-pass correct assessable expected words / assessable expected words. final_accuracy = expected words correct after accepted self-corrections / assessable expected words. A self-corrected word remains wrong for first-pass accuracy but becomes correct for final accuracy; the self-correction is also logged separately. Unresolved ASR tokens are excluded from both numerator and denominator until resolved.
oral_error_event_rule: OS3 ERROR EVENTS: substitution = first lexical attempt differs from expected token and is not an approved equivalent; omission = expected token has no aligned lexical attempt before the learner progresses beyond it; insertion = extra lexical token not aligned to any expected token; repetition = already-read expected word/phrase spoken again without textual need. A repeat used only to make an accepted self-correction is not an unnecessary repetition.
oral_self_correction_rule: OS4 SELF-CORRECTION: accepted when, without an app prompt, the learner replaces a confirmed misread/omission with the intended expected word within 5.0 seconds of the first erroneous attempt and before progressing more than 2 expected words beyond the target. Record correction_latency_seconds. The event still counts as a first-pass error, but the target counts correct in final_accuracy. RS07 may impose its stricter P-level latency/success threshold on top of this general acceptance rule.
oral_hesitation_rule: OS5 HESITATION: a long hesitation is a non-punctuation silence >2.0 seconds between assessable lexical events while the learner has not intentionally stopped. Measure from offset of the previous spoken lexical token to onset of the next spoken lexical token. Exclude permitted punctuation pauses, app/system audio, invalid recording gaps and ASR-uncertain spans. Filled pauses ('um', 'uh') extend the hesitation interval but are not insertions.
oral_restart_rule: OS6 FULL RESTART: after progressing at least 3 expected words into the current sentence, the learner returns to the sentence's first expected word or to an earlier sentence, producing a backward alignment jump of at least 3 expected tokens, without an app prompt. Repeating/correcting only 1–2 expected tokens is a local correction/repetition, not a full restart.
oral_punctuation_rule: OS7 PUNCTUATION: terminal eligible marks (. ? !) are compliant when the pause from final-word offset to next-word onset is 0.150–1.800 s and the next sentence begins without a boundary-linked omission. terminal_compliance = compliant eligible terminal marks / eligible terminal marks. Internal eligible marks (primarily comma, colon, semicolon) are compliant when the pause is 0.080–0.900 s and reading continues within the same sentence without a punctuation-triggered full restart. internal_compliance = compliant eligible internal marks / eligible internal marks. Exclude abbreviations, quoted punctuation or marks pre-tagged by the writer as non-pause-eligible.
oral_recovery_rule: OS8 CHALLENGE/UNFAMILIAR-WORD RECOVERY: computed only for writer-tagged recovery targets. recovery_time_seconds runs from onset of the learner's first attempt at the target to offset of the first accepted correct production. A target is recovered when it is correct or accepted-self-corrected within that RS/P time limit and the next 5 expected words contain no more than the allowed sequence errors and no target-triggered full restart. If the target is omitted with no attempt, recovery fails. If ASR is unresolved on the target, status is REASSESS rather than fail.
oral_wpm_rule: OS9 TIME/WPM: reading_time starts at onset of the first assessable passage word and ends at offset of the final assessable expected word reached. Include genuine hesitations, repetitions, self-corrections and restarts because they consume reading time; exclude app prompts/system audio and invalid recording gaps. text_WPM = number of expected passage words successfully progressed through / active elapsed reading minutes. Do not use total spoken-token count, because repetitions/insertions must not inflate WPM.
oral_asr_rule: OS10 ASR/ACCENT SAFEGUARD: ASR is evidence, not ground truth. Accent variation alone is never an error. A mismatch may be auto-scored as a child error only when the recognizer's confidence for the mismatching lexical hypothesis is at or above the engine's calibrated HIGH_CONFIDENCE threshold and no approved pronunciation/lexical equivalent applies. Lower-confidence mismatches are UNRESOLVED and excluded from scoring until a secondary recognition pass or replay resolves them. The deployed engine must freeze and version its HIGH_CONFIDENCE threshold; changing that threshold changes the scoring version.
oral_sample_validity_rule: OS11 SAMPLE VALIDITY: a metric is computable only when enough eligible evidence exists for that metric. If microphone dropout, clipping, overlapping speech, system narration or unresolved ASR removes >10% of expected words from assessability, the oral sample is INVALID for readiness scoring and must be reassessed. For a targeted metric requiring a minimum number of tagged opportunities, insufficient eligible targets yields REASSESS, not PASS or FAIL.

normalized_composite_rule: Optional full-round composite only after all 15 RS tracks have completed the same P level. Technical-invalid forms are REASSESS_TECHNICAL and do not count as valid attempts. All valid forms remain in the audit record; the system may never cherry-pick the best historical pass.
matched_form_equivalence_policy: EQUIV-2.1: exact 100 COUNT-100 words; World 1 one-word display; same RS/P10, scoring version, threshold version/status, comprehension blueprint class and safety/accessibility gates; fresh unseen content; non-compensatory global + RS-specific matching; candidate must pass all tolerances embedded in the canonical v0.22 Markdown specification.
readiness_attempt_policy: ATTEMPT-1.0: A readiness cycle is PRIMARY→CONFIRMATION. A valid failure ends that cycle. A new cycle may begin only after an intervening targeted learning block for that RS. After two consecutive failed/discordant valid cycles, set DIAGNOSTIC_HOLD and require at least two targeted non-readiness practice passages plus a documented diagnostic review before another readiness cycle. There is no unlimited back-to-back retry loop. Genuine later learning may reopen assessment after the required learning block.
readiness_cycle_status_rule: Readiness-cycle states: PRIMARY_PENDING; CONFIRMATION_PENDING; CONFIRMED_READY; NOT_YET; DISCORDANT_NOT_YET; REASSESS_TECHNICAL; INVALID_FORM; DIAGNOSTIC_HOLD. band_a_remediation_rule: After a valid failed/discordant cycle, remediate only that RS before a new cycle. The new cycle must use two fresh unseen EQUIV-2.1 matched P10 forms. personal_progress_measure: Primary comparison: RS11-P1 → RS11-P4. Report only this learner's within-competency metric changes; comprehension remains a separate measure. Cross-RS raw comparisons are prohibited.
hook_requirement: Open within first 25 words using mini mystery or an equally strong curiosity trigger; do not explain the lesson up front.
mid_passage_pull: By roughly the midpoint, introduce a change, clue, consequence, question or small complication so curiosity remains active.
ending_payoff: Resolve the passage cleanly in the final ~20 words; leave satisfaction, wonder or a useful thought—never a sermon or forced moral.
engagement_qa: Score Hook 0–2 + Mid-pull 0–2 + Payoff 0–2. Passage prose must score ≥5/6 and may not score 0 in any dimension.
qa_gate_definition: AMBIGUITY/FACT CONSISTENCY GATE: Every factual statement must be internally consistent with the premise and quiz. Every quiz item must have one defensible answer. Remove wording that permits multiple reasonable interpretations. Names, chronology, quantities, cause/effect and stated motivations must not contradict one another.
band_a_oral_readiness_rule: BAND-A ORAL READINESS (self-contained): readiness uses all RS01-P10…RS15-P10. Required P10 rules are the RS-specific success rules in this file. Core integrated minimums include: RS01 final_accuracy ≥97% and first_pass_accuracy ≥95%; RS02 ≤2 sequence errors with no 2+ word skip; RS06 ≤3 >2-second hesitations and no unexplained silence >6 s; RS08 ≤2 unnecessary repetition events and ≤1 full restart; RS11 pace_spread ≤0.25; RS13 middle-third accuracy within 2 percentage points of first-third with no 2+ word skip; RS14 final-third accuracy within 2 percentage points of first-third and final-third WPM no more than 15% below first-third; RS15 final_accuracy ≥95%, sequence_errors ≤2, long hesitations ≤4, full_restarts ≤1 and pace_spread ≤0.25. All remaining RS03–RS05, RS07, RS09–RS10 and RS12 P10 rules are equally mandatory; none may be bypassed by averaging.
factual_safety_requirement: AMBIGUITY/FACT CONSISTENCY GATE: Every factual statement must be internally consistent with the premise and quiz. Every quiz item must have one defensible answer. Remove wording that permits multiple reasonable interpretations. Names, chronology, quantities, cause/effect and stated motivations must not contradict one another.
babysteps_rule: Effortless learning: engaging first, gentle stretch, useful idea, no preaching, high chance of success.
prose_content_fidelity_rule: CONTENT FIDELITY: Preserve the row's core premise, knowledge strand, comprehension target, wisdom/trait intent, hook/pull/payoff intent, setting-accessibility requirement and QA flags. Prose may creatively realize the row, but it may not silently replace the learning objective.
prose_comprehension_evidence_rule: P4 PREDICTION: provide strong textual clues that make one next-event prediction clearly best; do not require guessing the author's imagination.
prose_oral_compatibility_rule: RS11 PACE CONSISTENCY: distribute difficulty evenly across the four passage quartiles; do not place nearly all difficult words or dialogue in one quarter.
prose_speech_fairness_rule: SPEECH/ACCENT FAIRNESS: The passage must be comfortable to read aloud by a beginner. Reject tongue-twister construction, dense alliteration, repeated minimal-pair traps, unnatural consonant clusters, clusters of difficult proper nouns, or wording chosen mainly to provoke ASR failure. Accent variation must not be used as a test. Names should be short/easy unless the passage itself gently teaches the name.
prose_vocabulary_rule: CONTROLLED STRETCH VOCABULARY: Most words must be familiar/decodable for a beginner reader. Stretch words must be intentional, context-supported and sparse enough that they do not break flow. Do not stack multiple unfamiliar words in one sentence. Writer-tagged RS05/RS12 targets count as the deliberate stretch; do not add extra difficult vocabulary merely to sound sophisticated.
prose_wisdom_rule: IMPLICIT WISDOM: The registry may name a trait or wisdom goal, but the prose should normally let it emerge from events, choices and consequences. Avoid formulaic moral endings such as 'X learned that...', 'X understood that...' or direct lectures unless the row specifically requires explicit explanation. A passage may be funny, mysterious, beautiful or surprising without stating a moral.
prose_duplicate_rule: NEARBY-DUPLICATE GATE: QA is performed in actual delivery-session order, not passage-ID order. Within the previous and next 15 delivered sessions, reject a near-duplicate core plot/event structure. A wisdom trait may recur only when conflict, setting and outcome are materially different. A hook type may recur only when the story/problem experience is clearly different. No passage may substantially duplicate the combination of plot + lesson/insight + hook/pull pattern of a nearby passage.
prose_confidence_rule: FIRST-100 CONFIDENCE PROTECTION (Sessions 41–60 — I understand): the passage must feel achievable on first encounter. No trick comprehension, humiliation/failure language, sudden difficulty spike, dense unfamiliar vocabulary, or punitive reread. Introduce at most one main new challenge beyond what the current RS/P cell requires. Feedback/remediation should preserve the learner's sense of 'I can do this' and desire for the next passage.
prose_wordcount_rhythm_rule: 100-WORD NATURALNESS: Final learner-visible prose must be exactly 100 words under the project's word-count convention, but exact count never justifies filler, clipped grammar, repeated meaning, awkward connectors, distorted facts, or unnatural oral rhythm. If the natural version is not 100 words, rewrite structurally rather than padding.
prose_quiz_path_rule: QUIZ/COMPREHENSION PATH: The finished passage and quiz must support exactly one defensible keyed answer per scored item. The intended evidence path must be visible in the text or strongly supported by it. Reject trick wording, unsupported inference, multiple reasonable answers, or a quiz whose correct answer depends on outside knowledge.
prose_effortless_learning_rule: BABYSTEPS EFFORTLESS-LEARNING GATE: The child should experience a worthwhile story/idea, not a disguised worksheet. Reading practice, vocabulary, wisdom and comprehension training should remain mostly invisible inside an engaging passage. A passage that is educational but dull, or entertaining but leaves no meaningful reading/comprehension value, fails.
prose_generation_gate_summary: PASS ONLY IF content fidelity + comprehension evidence + RS oral compatibility + speech/accent fairness + controlled vocabulary + implicit wisdom + nearby-duplicate check + confidence protection + exact-100 natural rhythm + one-defensible-answer quiz path + effortless-learning + engagement + all applicable factual/safety gates pass.
form_profile_lock_rule: P10 PRIMARY profile is frozen after prose QA and before learner exposure; CONFIRMATION must pass MFORM-1.1 against the frozen profile before delivery.
form_family_production_requirement: Production readiness requires the relevant RS P10 form family to be PRODUCTION_APPROVED in addition to individual candidate STRUCTURAL_EQUIV_PASS.
readiness_freshness_rule: Readiness evidence remains CURRENT until the first of: >56 calendar days since the latest passing same-RS confirmation/revalidation; >16 subsequent valid Band-A assessment/remediation sessions; or >28 consecutive calendar days with no SpeedReader learning session. Material scoring/threshold-version changes invalidate evidence immediately rather than merely making it stale. These numeric limits are PROVISIONAL_PILOT and require later calibration.
readiness_revalidation_rule: When evidence is REVALIDATION_DUE only because of recency/inactivity, use one fresh unseen EQUIV-2.1 same-RS P10 revalidation form. Score oral and comprehension streams independently before any targeted feedback. A passing stream renews only that stream's freshness anchor. A valid failing stream becomes NOT_YET and requires targeted remediation followed by a new full PRIMARY→CONFIRMATION cycle for that stream. Technical invalidity does not count as failure and does not reset freshness until valid evidence is obtained.
readiness_version_invalidation_rule: If OS/scoring semantics, threshold version/status, or another material measurement definition changes incompatibly, set VERSION_INVALIDATED. Do not use the one-form recency shortcut; require a new full two-form readiness cycle under the new compatible version.
band_a_evidence_current_rule: At final closure, the oral and comprehension readiness streams associated with all 15 RS positions must be CURRENT or CURRENT_REVALIDATED.
minimum_evidence_rule: P10 readiness minimums apply only to readiness/confirmation/revalidation forms.
form_minimum_precheck_rule: For P10 readiness forms, reject before learner exposure when writer-controlled tagged/event opportunities are below EVIDENCE-MIN-1.0.

rs_competency: Maintain a calm, reasonably even oral pace rather than rushing and stalling.
rs_observable_behavior: The learner's speed across the four quarters of the passage stays increasingly stable, after excluding punctuation pauses and unscored audio.
rs_measurement: Compute WPM for four equal assessable-word quartiles. pace_spread = (max quartile WPM - min quartile WPM) / median quartile WPM.
rs_success_rule: At P10: pace_spread ≤0.25 with no single quartile >35% slower than the learner's passage median. Absolute WPM is not compared with peers.
rs_readiness_evidence_rule: Use the valid same-RS P10 evidence defined by this row and the canonical Band-A readiness specification.
rs_readiness_status_rule: Use generic READY / BASELINE_MASTERY_CONFIRMED / REASSESS / NOT_YET states as applicable.
threshold_pilot_use: May guide coaching, remediation, and pilot eligibility to TRY Band B.
threshold_production_use: MUST NOT by itself issue PRODUCTION_BAND_A_READY or certification.
threshold_promotion_requirement: Requires a frozen calibration protocol, sufficient valid calibration evidence, equivalent-form stability analysis, decision-consistency analysis, predictive check against early Band-B performance, ASR/device/accent fairness review, borderline-case expert audit, and explicit QA approval.
rs_p1_to_p10_development: P1: Baseline quartile WPM profile only. | P2: pace_spread ≤0.50 or ≥10% improvement from baseline. | P3: ≤0.45. | P4: ≤0.42. | P5: ≤0.40. | P6: ≤0.36. | P7: ≤0.34. | P8: ≤0.30. | P9: ≤0.28. | P10: ≤0.25 and no quartile >35% below passage median.

oral_alignment_rule: OS1 ALIGNMENT: Score against learner-visible passage words in order. Normalize case and typographic apostrophes; retain punctuation separately for punctuation scoring. Use word-level sequence alignment over expected tokens and spoken lexical tokens. Non-lexical filled pauses such as 'um'/'uh' are hesitation events, not insertions. Approved lexical equivalents must be declared before scoring. A low-confidence ASR mismatch is UNRESOLVED, not automatically a child error.
oral_accuracy_rule: OS2 ACCURACY: first_pass_accuracy = first-pass correct assessable expected words / assessable expected words. final_accuracy = expected words correct after accepted self-corrections / assessable expected words. A self-corrected word remains wrong for first-pass accuracy but becomes correct for final accuracy; the self-correction is also logged separately. Unresolved ASR tokens are excluded from both numerator and denominator until resolved.
oral_error_event_rule: OS3 ERROR EVENTS: substitution = first lexical attempt differs from expected token and is not an approved equivalent; omission = expected token has no aligned lexical attempt before the learner progresses beyond it; insertion = extra lexical token not aligned to any expected token; repetition = already-read expected word/phrase spoken again without textual need. A repeat used only to make an accepted self-correction is not an unnecessary repetition.
oral_self_correction_rule: OS4 SELF-CORRECTION: accepted when, without an app prompt, the learner replaces a confirmed misread/omission with the intended expected word within 5.0 seconds of the first erroneous attempt and before progressing more than 2 expected words beyond the target. Record correction_latency_seconds. The event still counts as a first-pass error, but the target counts correct in final_accuracy. RS07 may impose its stricter P-level latency/success threshold on top of this general acceptance rule.
oral_hesitation_rule: OS5 HESITATION: a long hesitation is a non-punctuation silence >2.0 seconds between assessable lexical events while the learner has not intentionally stopped. Measure from offset of the previous spoken lexical token to onset of the next spoken lexical token. Exclude permitted punctuation pauses, app/system audio, invalid recording gaps and ASR-uncertain spans. Filled pauses ('um', 'uh') extend the hesitation interval but are not insertions.
oral_restart_rule: OS6 FULL RESTART: after progressing at least 3 expected words into the current sentence, the learner returns to the sentence's first expected word or to an earlier sentence, producing a backward alignment jump of at least 3 expected tokens, without an app prompt. Repeating/correcting only 1–2 expected tokens is a local correction/repetition, not a full restart.
oral_punctuation_rule: OS7 PUNCTUATION: terminal eligible marks (. ? !) are compliant when the pause from final-word offset to next-word onset is 0.150–1.800 s and the next sentence begins without a boundary-linked omission. terminal_compliance = compliant eligible terminal marks / eligible terminal marks. Internal eligible marks (primarily comma, colon, semicolon) are compliant when the pause is 0.080–0.900 s and reading continues within the same sentence without a punctuation-triggered full restart. internal_compliance = compliant eligible internal marks / eligible internal marks. Exclude abbreviations, quoted punctuation or marks pre-tagged by the writer as non-pause-eligible.
oral_recovery_rule: OS8 CHALLENGE/UNFAMILIAR-WORD RECOVERY: computed only for writer-tagged recovery targets. recovery_time_seconds runs from onset of the learner's first attempt at the target to offset of the first accepted correct production. A target is recovered when it is correct or accepted-self-corrected within that RS/P time limit and the next 5 expected words contain no more than the allowed sequence errors and no target-triggered full restart. If the target is omitted with no attempt, recovery fails. If ASR is unresolved on the target, status is REASSESS rather than fail.
oral_wpm_rule: OS9 TIME/WPM: reading_time starts at onset of the first assessable passage word and ends at offset of the final assessable expected word reached. Include genuine hesitations, repetitions, self-corrections and restarts because they consume reading time; exclude app prompts/system audio and invalid recording gaps. text_WPM = number of expected passage words successfully progressed through / active elapsed reading minutes. Do not use total spoken-token count, because repetitions/insertions must not inflate WPM.
oral_asr_rule: OS10 ASR/ACCENT SAFEGUARD: ASR is evidence, not ground truth. Accent variation alone is never an error. Lower-confidence mismatches are UNRESOLVED and excluded from scoring until a secondary recognition pass or replay resolves them. The deployed engine must freeze and version its HIGH_CONFIDENCE threshold; changing that threshold changes the scoring version.

oral_self_correction_rule: OS4 SELF-CORRECTION: accepted when, without an app prompt, the learner replaces a confirmed misread/omission with the intended expected word within 5.0 seconds of the first erroneous attempt and before progressing more than 2 expected words beyond the target. Record correction_latency_seconds. The event still counts as a first-pass error, but the target counts correct in final_accuracy. RS07 may impose its stricter P-level latency/success threshold on top of this general acceptance rule.
oral_hesitation_rule: OS5 HESITATION: a long hesitation is a non-punctuation silence >2.0 seconds between assessable lexical events while the learner has not intentionally stopped. Measure from offset of the previous spoken lexical token to onset of the next spoken lexical token. Exclude permitted punctuation pauses, app/system audio, invalid recording gaps and ASR-uncertain spans. Filled pauses ('um', 'uh') extend the hesitation interval but are not insertions.
oral_restart_rule: OS6 FULL RESTART: after progressing at least 3 expected words into the current sentence, the learner returns to the sentence's first expected word or to an earlier sentence, producing a backward alignment jump of at least 3 expected tokens, without an app prompt. Repeating/correcting only 1–2 expected tokens is a local correction/repetition, not a full restart.
oral_punctuation_rule: OS7 PUNCTUATION: terminal eligible marks (. ? !) are compliant when the pause from final-word offset to next-word onset is 0.150–1.800 s and the next sentence begins without a boundary-linked omission. terminal_compliance = compliant eligible terminal marks / eligible terminal marks. Internal eligible marks (primarily comma, colon, semicolon) are compliant when the pause is 0.080–0.900 s and reading continues within the same sentence without a punctuation-triggered full restart. internal_compliance = compliant eligible internal marks / eligible internal marks. Exclude abbreviations, quoted punctuation or marks pre-tagged by the writer as non-pause-eligible.
oral_recovery_rule: OS8 CHALLENGE/UNFAMILIAR-WORD RECOVERY: computed only for writer-tagged recovery targets. recovery_time_seconds runs from onset of the learner's first attempt at the target to offset of the first accepted correct production. A target is recovered when it is correct or accepted-self-corrected within that RS/P time limit and the next 5 expected words contain no more than the allowed sequence errors and no target-triggered full restart. If the target is omitted with no attempt, recovery fails. If ASR is unresolved on the target, status is REASSESS rather than fail.
oral_wpm_rule: OS9 TIME/WPM: reading_time starts at onset of the first assessable passage word and ends at offset of the final assessable expected word reached. Include genuine hesitations, repetitions, self-corrections and restarts because they consume reading time; exclude app prompts/system audio and invalid recording gaps. text_WPM = number of expected passage words successfully progressed through / active elapsed reading minutes. Do not use total spoken-token count, because repetitions/insertions must not inflate WPM.
oral_asr_rule: OS10 ASR/ACCENT SAFEGUARD: ASR is evidence, not ground truth. Accent variation alone is never an error. A mismatch may be auto-scored as a child error only when the recognizer's confidence for the mismatching lexical hypothesis is at or above the engine's calibrated HIGH_CONFIDENCE threshold and no approved pronunciation/lexical equivalent applies. Lower-confidence mismatches are UNRESOLVED and excluded from scoring until a secondary recognition pass or replay resolves them. The deployed engine must freeze and version its HIGH_CONFIDENCE threshold; changing that threshold changes the scoring version.
oral_sample_validity_rule: OS11 SAMPLE VALIDITY: a metric is computable only when enough eligible evidence exists for that metric. If microphone dropout, clipping, overlapping speech, system narration or unresolved ASR removes >10% of expected words from assessability, the oral sample is INVALID for readiness scoring and must be reassessed. For a targeted metric requiring a minimum number of tagged opportunities, insufficient eligible targets yields REASSESS, not PASS or FAIL.
oral_pipeline_order: OS12 PIPELINE ORDER: (1) validate audio/sample; (2) tokenize/normalize expected text; (3) align spoken lexical events; (4) mark substitutions/omissions/insertions/repetitions; (5) determine accepted self-corrections; (6) compute first_pass_accuracy and final_accuracy; (7) compute timing, hesitation, restart, punctuation, WPM and recovery metrics; (8) apply the assigned RS/P success rule; (9) apply ASR uncertainty/REASSESS rules before any readiness decision.

progress_display_rule: Child-facing progress uses native within-RS changes (for example accuracy +4 percentage points, hesitations 7→3, pace spread 0.42→0.28). Do not show one raw cross-RS 'improved by X%' score.

hook_requirement: Open within first 25 words using context clue or an equally strong curiosity trigger; do not explain the lesson up front.
mid_passage_pull: By roughly the midpoint, introduce a change, clue, consequence, question or small complication so curiosity remains active.
ending_payoff: Resolve the passage cleanly in the final ~20 words; leave satisfaction, wonder or a useful thought—never a sermon or forced moral.
engagement_qa: Score Hook 0–2 + Mid-pull 0–2 + Payoff 0–2. Passage prose must score ≥5/6 and may not score 0 in any dimension.
qa_gate_definition: AMBIGUITY/FACT CONSISTENCY GATE: Every factual statement must be internally consistent with the premise and quiz. Every quiz item must have one defensible answer. Remove wording that permits multiple reasonable interpretations. Names, chronology, quantities, cause/effect and stated motivations must not contradict one another.

Core integrated minimums include: RS01 final_accuracy ≥97% and first_pass_accuracy ≥95%; RS02 ≤2 sequence errors with no 2+ word skip; RS06 ≤3 >2-second hesitations and no unexplained silence >6 s; RS08 ≤2 unnecessary repetition events and ≤1 full restart; RS11 pace_spread ≤0.25; RS13 middle-third accuracy within 2 percentage points of first-third with no 2+ word skip; RS14 final-third accuracy within 2 percentage points of first-third and final-third WPM no more than 15% below first-third; RS15 final_accuracy ≥95%, sequence_errors ≤2, long hesitations ≤4, full_restarts ≤1 and pace_spread ≤0.25. factual_safety_requirement: AMBIGUITY/FACT CONSISTENCY GATE: Every factual statement must be internally consistent with the premise and quiz. Every quiz item must have one defensible answer. babysteps_rule: Effortless learning: engaging first, gentle stretch, useful idea, no preaching, high chance of success.
prose_content_fidelity_rule: CONTENT FIDELITY: Preserve the row's core premise, knowledge strand, comprehension target, wisdom/trait intent, hook/pull/payoff intent, setting-accessibility requirement and QA flags. Prose may creatively realize the row, but it may not silently replace the learning objective.
prose_comprehension_evidence_rule: P8 VOCABULARY IN CONTEXT: the target word's meaning must be inferable from nearby context without dictionary knowledge; include at least two useful context cues.
prose_oral_compatibility_rule: RS11 PACE CONSISTENCY: distribute difficulty evenly across the four passage quartiles; do not place nearly all difficult words or dialogue in one quarter.
prose_speech_fairness_rule: SPEECH/ACCENT FAIRNESS: The passage must be comfortable to read aloud by a beginner. Reject tongue-twister construction, dense alliteration, repeated minimal-pair traps, unnatural consonant clusters, clusters of difficult proper nouns, or wording chosen mainly to provoke ASR failure. Accent variation must not be used as a test. Names should be short/easy unless the passage itself gently teaches the name.
prose_vocabulary_rule: CONTROLLED STRETCH VOCABULARY: Most words must be familiar/decodable for a beginner reader. Stretch words must be intentional, context-supported and sparse enough that they do not break flow. Do not stack multiple unfamiliar words in one sentence. Writer-tagged RS05/RS12 targets count as the deliberate stretch; do not add extra difficult vocabulary merely to sound sophisticated.
prose_wisdom_rule: IMPLICIT WISDOM: The registry may name a trait or wisdom goal, but the prose should normally let it emerge from events, choices and consequences. Avoid formulaic moral endings such as 'X learned that...', 'X understood that...' or direct lectures unless the row specifically requires explicit explanation. A passage may be funny, mysterious, beautiful or surprising without stating a moral.
prose_duplicate_rule: NEARBY-DUPLICATE GATE: QA is performed in actual delivery-session order, not passage-ID order. Within the previous and next 15 delivered sessions, reject a near-duplicate core plot/event structure. A wisdom trait may recur only when conflict, setting and outcome are materially different. A hook type may recur only when the story/problem experience is clearly different. No passage may substantially duplicate the combination of plot + lesson/insight + hook/pull pattern of a nearby passage.
prose_confidence_rule: POST-100 STRENGTHENING (Sessions 101–150 — Strengthen and prepare for 200-word endurance): challenge may increase modestly, but difficulty must still rise gradually and remain compatible with beginner one-word reading. Do not sacrifice engagement, oral naturalness or comprehension uniqueness for toughness.
prose_wordcount_rhythm_rule: 100-WORD NATURALNESS: Final learner-visible prose must be exactly 100 words under the project's word-count convention, but exact count never justifies filler, clipped grammar, repeated meaning, awkward connectors, distorted facts, or unnatural oral rhythm. If the natural version is not 100 words, rewrite structurally rather than padding.
prose_quiz_path_rule: QUIZ/COMPREHENSION PATH: The finished passage and quiz must support exactly one defensible keyed answer per scored item. The intended evidence path must be visible in the text or strongly supported by it. Reject trick wording, unsupported inference, multiple reasonable answers, or a quiz whose correct answer depends on outside knowledge.
prose_effortless_learning_rule: BABYSTEPS EFFORTLESS-LEARNING GATE: The child should experience a worthwhile story/idea, not a disguised worksheet. Reading practice, vocabulary, wisdom and comprehension training should remain mostly invisible inside an engaging passage. A passage that is educational but dull, or entertaining but leaves no meaningful reading/comprehension value, fails.
prose_generation_gate_summary: PASS ONLY IF content fidelity + comprehension evidence + RS oral compatibility + speech/accent fairness + controlled vocabulary + implicit wisdom + nearby-duplicate check + confidence protection + exact-100 natural rhythm + one-defensible-answer quiz path + effortless-learning + engagement + all applicable factual/safety gates pass.
form_profile_lock_rule: P10 PRIMARY profile is frozen after prose QA and before learner exposure; CONFIRMATION must pass MFORM-1.1 against the frozen profile before delivery.
form_family_production_requirement: Production readiness requires the relevant RS P10 form family to be PRODUCTION_APPROVED in addition to individual candidate STRUCTURAL_EQUIV_PASS.
readiness_freshness_rule: Readiness evidence remains CURRENT until the first of: >56 calendar days since the latest passing same-RS confirmation/revalidation; >16 subsequent valid Band-A assessment/remediation sessions; or >28 consecutive calendar days with no SpeedReader learning session. band_a_evidence_current_rule: At final closure, the oral and comprehension readiness streams associated with all 15 RS positions must be CURRENT or CURRENT_REVALIDATED.
minimum_evidence_rule: P10 readiness minimums apply only to readiness/confirmation/revalidation forms.
form_minimum_precheck_rule: For P10 readiness forms, reject before learner exposure when writer-controlled tagged/event opportunities are below EVIDENCE-MIN-1.0.

rs_competency: Maintain a calm, reasonably even oral pace rather than rushing and stalling.
rs_observable_behavior: The learner's speed across the four quarters of the passage stays increasingly stable, after excluding punctuation pauses and unscored audio.
rs_measurement: Compute WPM for four equal assessable-word quartiles. pace_spread = (max quartile WPM - min quartile WPM) / median quartile WPM.

rs_readiness_status_rule: Use generic READY / BASELINE_MASTERY_CONFIRMED / REASSESS / NOT_YET states as applicable.
threshold_pilot_use: May guide coaching, remediation, and pilot eligibility to TRY Band B.
threshold_production_use: MUST NOT by itself issue PRODUCTION_BAND_A_READY or certification.
threshold_promotion_requirement: Requires a frozen calibration protocol, sufficient valid calibration evidence, equivalent-form stability analysis, decision-consistency analysis, predictive check against early Band-B performance, ASR/device/accent fairness review, borderline-case expert audit, and explicit QA approval.
